newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-EDWARDS DISMISSES MOVE FOR RAVANELLI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-EDWARDS DISMISSES MOVE FOR RAVANELLI.

text.p: Manchester United dismissed reports on Tuesday that they have launched a 10 million pounds ($16 million) bid to secure Italian striker Fabrizio Ravanelli from fellow premier club Middlesbrough.
The Italian news agency ANSA reported earlier in the day that United were offering $16 million to Middlesbrough and the same sum to Ravanelli for a four-year contract,
And the agency quoted Ravanelli as saying he would be interested in playing for the English champions.
But United's chief executive Martin Edwards dismissed the reports as "absolute nonsense.
"There is no foundation in these stories whatsoever. There have been no discussions with Middlesbrough and it came as a complete shock to get calls about them tonight," Edwards said.
Ravanelli cost Middlesbrough seven million pounds ($10.8 million) when he joined them from Juventus just weeks after helping them lift the European Cup last summer.

"The idea is exciting because Manchester United are prestigious," the grey-haired striker was reported as saying as he prepared at the Italian national team's training camp in Florence for upcoming World Cup qualifiers with Georgia and Moldova.
"The idea attracts me. Manchester United are more representative, they have greater ambitions, while Middlesbrough ... have a long-term programme.
"After you've won a lot, as I have, it's not easy to fight for a place in the UEFA Cup."

Ravanelli scored a hat-trick on his premiership debut against Liverpool and is the premier league's top scorer so Middlesbrough manager Bryan Robson, who built his career with United, would be unlikely to offload the man who has become extremely popular at the Teeside club.
He had been a key part of the club's massive rebuilding programme which has also seen the Brazilian trio of Juninho, Emerson and Branco brought in as well as England star Nick Barmby.
